lines.japanese: 「はーい」
lines.english: “Coming!”

lines.japanese: チャイムの音と共に立ちあがった小鳩が、ぱたたと玄関へ向かっていった。
lines.english: Kobato rose at the sound of the doorbell and pattered off toward the entryway.

lines.japanese: 「羽田さん、こんにちはー」
lines.english: “Hello, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「こんにちは。私ははるばるやって来た」
lines.english: “Hello. I have journeyed here from afar.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、アリスちゃんと吉川さん。いらっしゃーい」
lines.english: “Oh! Alice and Yoshikawa. Come on in!”

lines.japanese: 居間から顔を覗かせてみれば、大和撫子を体言したような緑なす黒髪と、はちみつ色のブロンドヘアーが並んでいた。
lines.english: I peeked out from the living room and saw a mane of glossy black hair, the very embodiment of a proper Japanese maiden, beside a head of honey-blonde.

lines.japanese: そして笑顔と無表情。まったく対象的なこのコンビは、吉川さんとアリスだ。
lines.english: One smiling, the other expressionless. This study in contrasts was Yoshikawa and Alice.

lines.japanese: 俺は生えてもいないエアー口ひげを整え、ジェントル然として迎えに出た。
lines.english: I groomed an imaginary mustache that wasn't there and went to greet them like a gentleman.

lines.japanese: たとえ起きあがるのが億劫でも、彼女らには礼を尽くさねばならない。
lines.english: However tiresome getting up might be, these two deserved every courtesy.

lines.japanese: 何故なら、我が家の小鳩は友達が少な──
lines.english: After all, our Kobato had so few frie—

lines.japanese: ──あ、いや、そうではなく。小鳩はあまりにも心身ともに美しい（おそらく世界でも一、二を争う）ので、同等のレベルで付きあえる女子となると、そう多くはないのだ。
lines.english: —No, that wasn't it. Kobato was so beautiful in both body and soul—probably one of the two loveliest people on Earth—that few girls existed on a high enough plane to associate with her as equals.

lines.japanese: そんな中、吉川さんとアリスは、かろうじて小鳩レベルの清らかさを持ちあわせている希少な人材だ。
lines.english: Of those few, Yoshikawa and Alice were rare specimens who just barely possessed Kobato-grade purity.

lines.japanese: 「やあ二人ともいらっしゃい！」
lines.english: “Welcome, you two!”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、お、お兄さんおはようございます」
lines.english: “Oh! G-good morning, Mr. Haneda.”

lines.japanese: うーん、相変わらず礼儀正しいなあ、吉川さんは。
lines.english: Hmm. Yoshikawa was as polite as ever.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、おはよう。相変わらずあなたはぱっとしない顔だ」
lines.english: “Good morning, Dora. Your face is as dull as ever.”

lines.japanese: そしてアリスは相変わらず無礼だなあ。思ったことをそのまま口に出すなんて、我が国の人間にはなかなか真似できないぞ、ははは。
lines.english: And Alice was as rude as ever. Speaking every thought that entered her head was a feat few people in this country could imitate. Ha ha ha.

lines.japanese: 「今日は遊びにきてくれたのかな？　我が家にはみかんくらいしか楽しみはないが、ささ、上がっておくれ」
lines.english: “Did you come over to play? This house has little to offer in the way of amusement besides mandarin oranges, but please, come in.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい、おじゃまします」
lines.english: “Th-thank you for having me.”

lines.japanese: 「私もこの家に上がるだろう。そしてやはりあなたはぱっとしない顔だ」
lines.english: “I shall enter this house. And your face remains dull as ever.”

lines.japanese: 「うるさい、余計な慣用句ばっかり覚えやがって。でも倒置法が抜けて、だいぶ日本語上手になってきたね」
lines.english: “Oh, shut up. You only learn useless expressions. But you've stopped inverting every sentence, so your Japanese really is getting better.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、私は優秀だ。貴様とは違う」
lines.english: “Yes. I am exceptional. Unlike you.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと、みかんあげないぞ」
lines.english: “Why, you... No mandarins for you.”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん、そういうイジワルはよくないよ」
lines.english: “Big Brother, don't be mean.”

lines.japanese: なぜか俺は怒られた。
lines.english: Somehow, I was the one who got scolded.

lines.japanese: 「あ、じゃあふたりとも、テレビの部屋に来てもらっていい？　ひろい部屋でやろうよ」
lines.english: “Oh, could both of you come into the TV room? Let's work somewhere with more space.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ありがとー」
lines.english: “Sure. Thanks!”

lines.japanese: 「今日は私も参加します」
lines.english: “I shall also participate today.”

lines.japanese: 「よし、それじゃお兄ちゃんも参加しちゃうぞ」
lines.english: “All right! Big Brother's joining in too.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 何が始まるのかは知らないけど、とりあえず付いていこうとしたら予想外の難色を示された。
lines.english: I had no idea what they were starting, but when I tried to tag along, I met with an unexpectedly unenthusiastic response.

lines.japanese: 「えっ、お兄ちゃんも……？」
lines.english: “You too, Big Brother...?”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、ダメ？」
lines.english: “Oh. Am I not allowed?”

lines.japanese: 「ダメじゃないけど……」
lines.english: “It's not that...”

lines.japanese: あれ、あれれれれ。小鳩が俺のことを拒否している？
lines.english: Wait. Wait, wait, wait. Was Kobato rejecting me?

lines.japanese: あっ、そうか。年頃の女の子だもんな、友達と遊ぶのにお兄ちゃんも一緒だなんてちょっと嫌だよな。
lines.english: Oh, of course. She was a girl at that age. It was only natural she'd rather not have her big brother tagging along while she hung out with friends.

lines.japanese: いやはや、これは配慮が足らなかった。うん、これは女の子なら普通のことなんだ。だから決して、俺が嫌われているわけじゃないんだよ。そうだよ、そうだよ。
lines.english: Goodness, how thoughtless of me. Yes, any girl would feel that way. It certainly didn't mean she hated me. Of course not. Of course not.

lines.japanese: 「う、うん、ごめんな。お兄ちゃんその、アレだ。ちょっと居間に取りにいきたいものがあったんだ。だからべつに、混ぜてもらおうなんて思ってなかったよ。寂しくなんか全然ないよ」
lines.english: “R-right, sorry. Big Brother just, um... needed to get something from the living room. I wasn't hoping you'd let me join you. I'm not lonely at all.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああーっ。そ、そじゃないよ。えっと、吉川さんと部活の課題やろうと思ってたから」
lines.english: “Oh! N-no, that's not what I meant. Um, Yoshikawa and I were going to work on something for our club.”

lines.japanese: 「へ？　部活？」
lines.english: “Huh? Your club?”

lines.japanese: 小鳩の部活動……って、何だったっけ。ちょっとタカシの記憶でも探ってみよ──
lines.english: Kobato's club... What was it again? Let me dig through Takashi's memories for a—

lines.japanese: 「吉川さん、お兄ちゃんいっしょでもいい？」
lines.english: “Yoshikawa, is it okay if my brother joins us?”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん。ちょっと恥ずかしいけど、羽田さんのお兄さんなら」
lines.english: “Y-yes. It's a little embarrassing, but if it's your brother...”

lines.japanese: 「だって。じゃあいっしょに行こう、お兄ちゃん」
lines.english: “She says it's okay. Let's go together, Big Brother.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　あ、ああ。じゃあお邪魔します」
lines.english: “Hmm? Oh, sure. Don't mind if I do.”

lines.japanese: 「たこつぼさん、このスクリーントーンちょっともらっていい？」
lines.english: “Octopot, can I have a little of this screentone?”

lines.japanese: 「うんいいよ。あ、トリニダードさん花柄トーン使うんだ。これかわいいよねー」
lines.english: “Sure. Oh, Trinidad, you're using the flower pattern? This one's cute, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。貼るばしょなくても使いたくなっちゃうよねー」
lines.english: “Yeah. It makes you want to use it even when you have nowhere to put it.”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん」
lines.english: “Mm-hmm.”

lines.japanese: 四人で囲んだちゃぶ台の上、原稿用紙が所狭しと並べられていた。
lines.english: Sheets of manuscript paper covered every inch of the low table around which the four of us sat.

lines.japanese: その上にペンを走らせるのは、互いをことさらにペンネームで呼びあう二人。
lines.english: Two girls moved their pens across the pages, conspicuously addressing each other by their pen names.

lines.japanese: 俺は小動物アリスの金髪をグルーミングしながら、なかば呆然とその様子を眺めていた。
lines.english: I stared at them in something of a daze while grooming the little blond creature named Alice.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだ。ここのセリフ変えた方がいいかなって思ってたんだけど、たこつぼさんどう思う？」
lines.english: “Oh, right. I was thinking of changing the dialogue here. What do you think, Octopot?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　うーん、私はトリニダードさんっぽくて好きだけどな」
lines.english: “Hmm? I don't know. I like it. It sounds like you, Trinidad.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、そうかなあ」
lines.english: “Hmm. You think so?”

lines.japanese: ええ、そうでした。そういえば漫画研究部の所属でしたっけねえ、この子たち。
lines.english: Oh, right. Come to think of it, these girls were in the manga club.

lines.japanese: 俺は傍らの完成原稿を盗み見ながら、タカシの記憶を探る。
lines.english: I sneaked a look at the finished pages beside me and searched Takashi's memories.

lines.japanese: 襖の開いた部屋の奥で、ひとり机に向かっている小鳩の姿。
lines.english: Kobato sitting alone at her desk in the room beyond an open sliding door.

lines.japanese: あの頃は小鳩も兄に甘えきれず、どこか親戚みたいな関係だった。
lines.english: Back then, Kobato hadn't been able to depend fully on her brother. Their relationship had felt almost like distant relatives.

lines.japanese: だから俺──タカシであった俺は、興味のある分野ながら、ついつい声掛けをためらっていたのだ。
lines.english: And so I—the me who had been Takashi—had hesitated to speak to her, despite my interest in the subject.

lines.japanese: しかし、いまの俺たちは違う。タカシの知識に、その他大勢の度胸や図々しさが加わった、無敵のスーパーお兄ちゃんなのだ。
lines.english: But things were different now. Takashi's knowledge had been joined by the courage and shamelessness of everybody else, making me the invincible Super Big Brother.

lines.japanese: 「二人とも！　なにか俺に手伝えることはないかい？」
lines.english: “You two! Is there anything I can do to help?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ？」
lines.english: “Wh-what?”

lines.japanese: 彼女たちは原稿用紙から顔を上げ、ぽかんとした顔で俺を見た。
lines.english: They raised their heads from the manuscript paper and stared blankly at me.

lines.japanese: 「さあなんでも言ってくれ！　俺はいつだってみんなの役に立ちたいんだ」
lines.english: “Go on, ask me anything! I'm always happy to make myself useful.”

lines.japanese: 俺は両手を広げて協力を申しでた。だというのに、ふたりは未だぽかん顔継続中だ。
lines.english: I spread my arms and offered my assistance. Yet the two of them continued to stare.

lines.japanese: 「え、ええええ？　そ、そんな、だって……な、何いきなり」
lines.english: “Wh-what? B-but... Where did that come from?”

lines.japanese: 「なにって、こう見えてもこの俺、ＰＮ聖☆ヨージんは漫画には詳しいんだぞ。なにか出来ることがあれば言ってくれよ」
lines.english: “Why, despite appearances, I, the artist known as Saint☆Youjin, know my manga. Just tell me if there's anything I can do.”

lines.japanese: 「は、恥ずかしいとはこういうことだ……」
lines.english: “S-so this is what embarrassment feels like...”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい。お兄さんに見られるのは恥ずかしいです」
lines.english: “Y-yes. It would be embarrassing to have you look at it, Mr. Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「恥ずかしいって……」
lines.english: “Embarrassing...?”

lines.japanese: さっきから目の前に広げてるじゃないか。見られたくないなんて、何を今更なこと言ってるんだ、この子たちは。
lines.english: They'd had it spread out in front of me this whole time. Why start saying they didn't want me to see it now?

lines.japanese: なんて思いつつ首を傾げていたら、アリスが俺の手にブラシを握らせる。
lines.english: As I tilted my head at the thought, Alice pressed the brush into my hand.

lines.japanese: 「あなたは女ゴコロを生涯理解できないだろう。もちろん私のココロもだ」
lines.english: “You will never understand a woman's heart for as long as you live. Mine, of course, is included.”

lines.japanese: 金髪少女は得意顔で言うと、ブラシごと俺の手首を掴んで自分の頭へ載せた。
lines.english: The blond girl spoke with a smug look, then took my wrist—brush and all—and set my hand atop her head.

lines.japanese: 命じられるがまま毛繕いを再開しながら、俺はなんとか小鳩たちの力になろうと考える。
lines.english: I resumed grooming her as ordered and tried to think of some way to help Kobato and Yoshikawa.

lines.japanese: ふむ……「見られる」のが嫌だと言うならば……
lines.english: Hmm... If they didn't want me “looking” at the art...

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ絵の方じゃなくて、話の方ならどうだい？」
lines.english: “Then how about the story instead of the pictures?”
“The story?”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん。ストーリーで何か参考にしたいことがあれば、何でも聞いてくれ」
lines.english: “Sure. If there's anything you need inspiration for, ask me whatever you like.”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん、まんがの話って作れるの？」
lines.english: “Can you come up with stories for manga, Big Brother?”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ！　このスケールの大きさが太陽を超えたとまで言われた俺に、出来ないことなんかあるはずないじゃないか。じゃあ、どんな話を書いてるのかだけでも教えてくれ」
lines.english: “What?! You think anything could be beyond a man of such grand scale it's said he surpasses the sun itself? At least tell me what sort of story you're writing.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、でもいま描いてるの……ね？」
lines.english: “Umm, but what we're drawing now is... You know?”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん、お兄さんってこういうジャンルとか読まなそう……」
lines.english: “Y-yeah. You don't seem like you'd read this kind of thing, Mr. Haneda...”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ、どうしたんだ？　なんでそんな困り顔なんだ？」
lines.english: “What is it? Why do both of you look so troubled?”

lines.japanese: 微妙に目を逸らすふたり。大袈裟に覗きこもうとしても、いちいち目が泳ぐ。
lines.english: They kept looking away. Every time I made a show of leaning in to catch their eyes, their gazes darted aside.

lines.japanese: 「そんなに不安そうな顔をすることないだろ……」
lines.english: “You don't have to look so worried...”

lines.japanese: 「分かった、それじゃ系統だけでも教えてくれ、俺に相談したくないジャンルってなんだい？」
lines.english: “All right, just tell me the genre. What kind of story could you possibly not want my advice on?”

lines.japanese: 「れんあいもの」
lines.english: “Romance.”
“Whaaat?!”

lines.japanese: とんでもない言いがかりに俺は憤りを覚えた。アリスと一緒に立ちあがる。
lines.english: Incensed by this outrageous accusation, I rose to my feet. Alice stood with me.

lines.japanese: なんだ、どういうことだ。恋愛面において頼りにされないとは、男としての不名誉だ。
lines.english: What was the meaning of this? To be deemed unreliable in matters of love was an affront to my manhood.

lines.japanese: 俺は共に立ちあがったアリスへ空のコップを手渡し、おかわりを頼んで台所へ向かわせた。
lines.english: I handed my empty glass to Alice, who had risen with me, asked for a refill, and sent her off to the kitchen.

lines.japanese: 「なんだと、恋愛ものでお兄ちゃんに相談できないとはどういうことだ。理由如何では、お兄ちゃんただでは済まさないぞ」
lines.english: “What do you mean you can't ask Big Brother about romance? Depending on your answer, Big Brother may have to take drastic measures.”

lines.japanese: 「ただでは済まさないって、なにするの？」
lines.english: “What kind of drastic measures?”

lines.japanese: 「具体的には、今日の夕飯にピーマンが入ってたら全部小鳩の皿へ移します」
lines.english: “To be specific, if there are bell peppers with dinner tonight, I will transfer all of mine to Kobato's plate.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんとー」
lines.english: “Wh-what a calamity!”

lines.japanese: 「さあ、どうするんだ。このままでは我が家の夕食に悲劇の波が訪れるぞ。きちんとお兄ちゃんを頼れない理由を説明しなさい」
lines.english: “Well? At this rate, a tide of tragedy shall descend upon our dinner table. Now explain why you refuse to rely on Big Brother.”

lines.japanese: 「ちがっ、違うよ。頼りにならないとか、そ、そゆことじゃなくて」
lines.english: “No! That's not it. It's not that we can't rely on you, or anything like that.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩はあわわと両手を振りだした。ああ、うちの小鳩は慌てる姿もかわいいなあ……あ、いやいや、俺べつにシスコンとかロリコンとかそういうの全然ないけどね。
lines.english: Kobato flailed both hands in panic. Ah, even a flustered Kobato was adorable... N-no, but I don't have a sister complex or a Lolita complex or anything.

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうじゃなくて……」
lines.english: “It's just...”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、じゃあお兄ちゃんそういう、その……したことあるのっ？」
lines.english: “W-well, have you ever actually, um... done it, Big Brother?”

lines.japanese: 「へっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: そういう……って、つまりその、恋愛か？
lines.english: Done it... Meaning romance, presumably?
“Mrrr...”

lines.japanese: トリニダードさんは珍しく反撃してきたあと、顔を真っ赤にして俺を睨んでいた。
lines.english: Trinidad, mounting a rare counterattack, glared at me with a face gone scarlet.
“Ahhh...”

lines.japanese: たこつぼさんまで俺の顔を見上げていた。
lines.english: Even Octopot was looking up at me now.

lines.japanese: 「そ、そりゃまあ……お兄ちゃんだからね。まあそれなりにね。恋愛経験くらいはあるよね」
lines.english: “W-well... I am your big brother. I've had my share. Of course I've got some romantic experience.”

lines.japanese: 「自慢みたいになるからあまり言わないけどね。ひとたび街を歩けば誰もほっとかないよね。まあね、今だってね、それなりに恋愛してるよね」
lines.english: “I don't talk about it much because it sounds like bragging, but I can't walk down the street without people taking an interest in me. Why, even now, I'm enjoying a certain degree of romance.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩に見栄を張りたい一心から、俺は世迷言を並べたてた。
lines.english: In my overwhelming desire to impress Kobato, I piled absurdity upon absurdity.

lines.japanese: 「えっ、誰かと付きあったことあるの？」
lines.english: “You've gone out with somebody before?”

lines.japanese: 「ないよ」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: しかし裏切りたくない一心から真実を告げていた。
lines.english: But in my overwhelming desire never to betray her, I told the truth.

lines.japanese: 「じゃっ、じゃあ、いま好きなひとは居るんですか？」
lines.english: “Th-then, is there someone you like now?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、それはもちろん小ば──」
lines.english: “Oh, of course. Koba—”

lines.japanese: 「──って、言えるかあああっ！」
lines.english: “—Like I could tell you!”

lines.japanese: 「所詮あなたはその程度の男ね」
lines.english: “In the end, you are only that much of a man.”

lines.japanese: 「あ。アリス」
lines.english: “Oh. Alice.”

lines.japanese: 「小鳩とあきらは安心してください。私はその男よりも豊富な恋愛経験を持っています。きっとあなたたちの話作りに役立つことでしょう」
lines.english: “Kobato and Akira, be at ease. I possess far more romantic experience than that man. I am certain it will aid you in constructing your story.”

lines.japanese: 「へー、アリスちゃん人気あるんだ。すごーい」
lines.english: “Wow, Alice, you must be popular. Amazing.”

lines.japanese: 「当たり前です。今後私にはラブレターなども寄せられるはずだ」
lines.english: “Naturally. In the future, I am certain to receive love letters and the like.”

lines.japanese: 「わー、アリスちゃんすごいすごーい。子供だけど大人ー」
lines.english: “Wow, Alice, that's amazing. You're a child, but you're a grown-up.”

lines.japanese: 「それでは私に魅了されて止まない、ある無職の男たちの話をします」
lines.english: “Then I shall tell you of certain unemployed men who are helplessly enthralled by me.”

lines.japanese: 「その男たちはいつも駅前でぶらぶらと歩いているだけの毎日を送っていました。一人は俳優という見果てぬ夢を追いかけるロクデナシィ。そしてもう一人はなんの夢もないロクデナシィでした」
lines.english: “Those men spent their days doing nothing but loitering around the station. One was a good-for-nothing chasing the hopeless dream of becoming an actor. The other was a good-for-nothing with no dream at all.”

lines.japanese: 「すごーい、アリスちゃんたち三角形だー」
lines.english: “Amazing, Alice. You three are a love triangle.”

lines.japanese: 「それでそれで？　一緒に帰ったりしたの？　二人で喫茶店いったりするの？」
lines.english: “And then what? Did you walk home together? Did you two go to a café?”

lines.japanese: お話の中でロクデナシィは言われたい放題だったが、俺はツッコミも入れずにおとなしくうんうん聞いていた。
lines.english: The good-for-nothings in her tale were taking quite a beating, but I sat quietly and listened without a single retort.

lines.japanese: 恋愛経験を問われたとき、わずかながら心に引っかかるものがあったのだ。
lines.english: Something had caught faintly in my mind when they asked about my romantic experience.

lines.japanese: 恋愛経験──
lines.english: Romantic experience—

lines.japanese: ──どうなんだろう。たしかに、ないと言えばない。
lines.english: —What did that amount to, really? I certainly had none, in one sense.

lines.japanese: ひょっとしたら俺は、その経験不足がゆえ、妹に対する真摯な想いを妙な方向へ履き違えがちなのだろうか。
lines.english: Could my lack of experience be why I kept mistaking my sincere feelings for my sister for something strange?

lines.japanese: ちなみにアリスの恋愛譚は、俺とプラチナがアリスを取りあい、拳で争うところまで発展した。
lines.english: Incidentally, Alice's love story grew until Platinum and I were fighting with our fists for her hand.

lines.japanese: 俺は気位の高い金髪娘が自尊心を損なわぬよう、やつがくだらないジャパニーズ指ゲームでムキになっていたことを内緒にしておいてやった。
lines.english: To preserve the proud blond girl's dignity, I kept quiet about how heated she had actually gotten over a silly Japanese finger game.

lines.japanese: 台所からは水道音が聞こえてくる。
lines.english: I heard water running in the kitchen.

lines.japanese: 『いやほんと久しぶりだよね。つか何年ぶり？　俺もうみんなの顔忘れかけてたもん』
lines.english: “Wow, it really has been a while. How many years? I'd almost forgotten everybody's faces.”

lines.japanese: 『やめてよ、なに言ってるんだよ。まるで僕たち仲悪いみたいじゃない。昨日フツーに一緒の番組出てるし』
lines.english: “Oh, stop. What are you talking about? You're making it sound like we don't get along. We were on the same show yesterday.”

lines.japanese: テレビは環境音代わりに点けていた。ミドル世代の芸能人を集めて、若手芸人がイジくり倒すバラエティみたいだが、ほとんど観てはいなかった。
lines.english: The TV was on for background noise. It looked like one of those variety shows where young comedians mercilessly rib a collection of middle-aged celebrities, but I had hardly been watching.

lines.japanese: ご近所様から家庭的な香りが漂ってきた時間帯、吉川さんとアリスは丁寧に頭を下げて帰っていった。
lines.english: Around the time the comforting smell of home cooking began drifting in from the neighbors, Yoshikawa and Alice bowed politely and went home.

lines.japanese: デートに出かけた叔父さんと叔母さんが戻ってくるまでは、あと一時間ぐらいあるだろう。
lines.english: There was probably another hour before Uncle and Auntie returned from their date.

lines.japanese: その間、俺は寝転がって天井を見上げながら、また今日もあのことを考えていた。
lines.english: In the meantime, I lay on my back and stared at the ceiling, thinking yet again about that matter.

lines.japanese: あの夜──あのイブの夜、俺たちは互いの想いを伝えあった。
lines.english: That night—Christmas Eve—we had told each other how we felt.

lines.japanese: しかし、だからこそいまは、あえて兄妹でいることを選んだ。
lines.english: And precisely because of that, we had chosen for now to remain brother and sister.

lines.japanese: まだ視野の狭い俺たちは、この小さな家の外をもっと知らねばならない。
lines.english: Our perspective was still narrow. We needed to learn more of the world outside this little house.

lines.japanese: 互いを愛する気持ちが、幼さゆえの勘違いではないと知るためにも。
lines.english: If only to know that our love for each other was not a childish misunderstanding.

lines.japanese: だけどよく考えたら、いまの俺は広い世界どころか、相変わらず一にも小鳩、二も小鳩の視野狭窄だ。あ、もちろん俺、ロリコンとかシスコンとかではないけどね。
lines.english: But when I thought about it, my vision hadn't widened at all. It was still Kobato first and Kobato second. And of course, I don't have a Lolita complex or a sister complex or anything.

lines.japanese: うーむ、このままでは、せっかく兄妹に戻ったってのに進歩がないな。意識的に視野を広げる必要がありそうだ。
lines.english: Hmm. At this rate, going back to being siblings would accomplish nothing. I needed to make a conscious effort to broaden my perspective.

lines.japanese: そうだな、身近なところで、俺の大好きな森里君を例に考えてみよう。
lines.english: All right. Let me use my beloved Morisato as a familiar example.

lines.japanese: 彼の場合、まず羽田タカシとはお互いを尊敬しあうような、優しい関係を育んでいた（※感想には個人差があります）。
lines.english: In his case, he had first cultivated a gentle relationship of mutual respect with Takashi Haneda. (Opinions may vary.)

lines.japanese: その一方で、成田隼人とは躊躇なく叱責しあえるような、冷静な関係を築いていた。
lines.english: At the same time, he had built a sober relationship with Hayato Narita, in which they could admonish one another without hesitation.

lines.japanese: そしてこれらが合わさったとき、途端にただの友人ではなく、大親友とも呼ぶべき関係にまで発展した。
lines.english: When those two relationships came together, they immediately developed beyond mere friendship into what could only be called a bond between best friends.

lines.japanese: ふむ……つまり、ひとりの人間をより分かろうとするなら、様々な視点を持つことが肝要なのかもしれない。
lines.english: Hmm... In other words, if I wanted to understand one person more fully, perhaps the key was to approach them from a variety of perspectives.

lines.japanese: よし、今日から俺は、広い意識を持って行動するぞ。
lines.english: All right. From this day forward, I would act with a broader awareness.

lines.japanese: そう心がけることで、自分や小鳩やその他さまざまが、いまとは違う風に見えてくるかもしれない。
lines.english: With that in mind, I might begin to see myself, Kobato, and all sorts of other things in a new light.

lines.japanese: おお、なんだか力が湧いてきたぞ。
lines.english: Oh! I could feel strength welling within me.

lines.japanese: 俺はふつふつと燃えたつこの感動を、全身Ｘの字に伸ばすことで表現した。
lines.english: I expressed the emotion simmering through my body by stretching all four limbs into a giant X.

lines.japanese: 「生きてるって素晴らしいィィィ！」
lines.english: “What a wonderful thing it is to be aliiiive!”

lines.japanese: 「はひゃっ！？　な、なに？　どしたのお兄ちゃん」
lines.english: “Eep! Wh-what? What's wrong, Big Brother?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ小鳩！　俺はいま自分の到達点がはっきりして、燃えていたところなんだ。さあ小鳩も一緒に熱くなろう！」
lines.english: “Oh, Kobato! I have just seen my destination clearly, and my soul is on fire! Come, Kobato! Let us burn together!”

lines.japanese: 「わか、分かったから叫ばないで。ご近所さんに迷惑だから」
lines.english: “O-okay, but stop shouting. You'll bother the neighbors.”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、なにを寂しいことを言ってるんだ小鳩。ほら見なさい、フリッキー５のヨッくんも言っているだろう。アゲるときアゲてかないと、人生なんてつまらない――」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha! What a lonely thing to say, Kobato. Listen, even Yoshi of Fricky Five says it: if you don't raise the roof when it's time to party, life's no fun—”

lines.japanese: 『あ、どもども～。皆さんお元気っすかあ？』
lines.english: “Ah, hello, hellooo. How's everybody doing?”

lines.japanese: 「――って、えええっ！？　ヨッくんテレビ出てる！？」
lines.english: “—Wait, whaaat?! Yoshi's on TV?!”

lines.japanese: 画面の向こうは店頭ロケの風景。ミュージックショップをバックに、若作りした男性タレントが五人並んでいる。
lines.english: On the screen was an on-location shoot outside a store. Five men who dressed too young for their age stood in a row before a music shop.

lines.japanese: ん？　よく見りゃあの店は、アルバトロスの中にあるＣＤ屋じゃないか。あ、あれ？　ていうことは！？
lines.english: Hmm? On closer inspection, wasn't that the CD store inside the Albatross? W-wait. Did that mean...?!

lines.japanese: 「えっ、嘘！？　ヨッくん……っていうかフリッキー５が柳木原に来てんの？」
lines.english: “What? No way! Yoshi... I mean, Fricky Five are here in Yanagihara?!”

lines.japanese: フリッキー５。それはかつて一世を風靡した、伝説のアイドルグループ。
lines.english: Fricky Five: the legendary idol group that had once taken the nation by storm.

lines.japanese: 昨年から引きつづき、いまだチャートに引っかかっている、彼らの復刻版ベストアルバム「ロシアン妊娠検査薬」。
lines.english: Their reissued greatest-hits album, *Russian Pregnancy Test*, had remained on the charts since the previous year.

lines.japanese: その地味なロングセールが引き金となって、いま、お母さん世代を中心に局所的な再ブームを呼んでいるらしい。
lines.english: Apparently its modest but steady sales had sparked a small, localized revival, especially among women of my mother's generation.

lines.japanese: しかし、まさかあのフリファが、俺たちの街ギバラに来るなんて……。
lines.english: But I never dreamed the Frickies would come to our town, Gibara...

lines.japanese: 『フリッキー５の足利美樹ですコンバンワ！　ゴールデンタイムにお邪魔するのも久しぶりですコンバンワ！』
lines.english: “I’m Yoshiki Ashikaga of Fricky Five—good evening! Been a while since we dropped in on prime time—good evening!”

lines.japanese: コンバンワ！
lines.english: Good evening!

lines.japanese: うーむ、よくよく思いだしてみれば、さっき喋ってたのはマサシと殿下だったのか。俺としたことが、ぼんやりしてて聞きながしてしまうとは。
lines.english: Hmm. Now that I really thought back, those voices earlier must have been Masashi and His Highness. How could I have let them wash over me without noticing?

lines.japanese: ま、さすがにヨッくんの声だけは聞きのがさないけどね！
lines.english: Not that I would ever miss Yoshi's voice!

lines.japanese: 『今日は僕たちの“ロシアン妊娠検査薬”を全国で一番売ってくれた、柳木原のＣＤショップに来てるんですけどね』
lines.english: “Today we're visiting the Yanagihara CD shop that sold more copies of our *Russian Pregnancy Test* than any other store in the country.”

lines.japanese: 「店員さんたちが頑張ってくれたお陰で、僕ら当時の衣装着る羽目になっちゃって。なんですか、このちぐはぐ感。僕らこれ、ギャグじゃないんですよ？　真面目にやってんですよ？」
lines.english: “Thanks to all the hard work from the staff, we've ended up having to wear our old costumes again. What is this mismatched mess? This isn't a joke, you know. We're doing this seriously.”

lines.japanese: 「なにしろ今週末には、ミニコンサートまで開いてくれるらしくて。僕らいまでも全盛期の動きできるか、チョー心配なんですよもォー！」
lines.english: “And apparently they're even holding a mini-concert for us this weekend. Now we're all suuuper worried whether we can still move like we did in our prime!”

lines.japanese: 「週末にコンサート！？」
lines.english: “A concert this weekend?!”

lines.japanese: 行きたい！
lines.english: I had to go!

lines.japanese: ななな、なんてことだ。そんな情報ぜんぜん聞いてなかった。たたた、大変だ、一大事にござる……！
lines.english: Wh-wh-what a calamity. I hadn't heard a word about this. Th-th-this was an emergency of the highest order...!

lines.japanese: 「こここコヴァッ、コバ、コバババコバ、聞いたか、い、いい、今すぐ予約せねヴァ、一緒にコンサート行こう！」
lines.english: “K-K-Koba, Koba, Kobababakoba! Did you h-hear that? We have to reserve tickets right now! Let's go to the concert together!”

lines.japanese: 「それじゃチケットの予約は番組のＨＰから！　アクセスはこちらのＱＲコード――」
lines.english: “To reserve tickets, visit the show's website! Scan this QR code—”

lines.japanese: 「ケータイ！」
lines.english: “My phone!”

lines.japanese: 俺は慌てて充電ホルダーに飛びつく──
lines.english: I lunged for the charging cradle—

lines.japanese: 「あ、そだ。うにうに出てる番組やってた」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Uni-Uni's show is on.”

lines.japanese: ──一方、小鳩はチャンネルを変えていた。
lines.english: —while Kobato changed the channel.

lines.japanese: 「リモコンよこしなさい」
lines.english: “Hand over the remote.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うにうにが出てる間はやだ」
lines.english: “N-no. Not while Uni-Uni's on.”

lines.japanese: そしてうにうにが画面から消えるころ、すでにフリファの一般チケット予約は終わっていましたとさ。
lines.english: And by the time Uni-Uni disappeared from the screen, general ticket reservations for the Frickies had already closed.

lines.japanese: めでたしめでたし。
lines.english: And they all lived happily ever after.

lines.japanese: めでたくねぇー！
lines.english: Nothing about this was happy!
